grammar_concept.title: Used to + base verb
grammar_concept.rule: Use "used to" + base verb for repeated actions or states that were true in the past but are not true now. It only exists in the past — there is no present form.
grammar_concept.simple_explanation: "Used to" descreve um hábito ou estado que era verdade no passado mas já não é agora — não existe "use to" no presente, só serve para comparar o passado com o presente.
grammar_concept.example: I used to live in Lisbon, but now I live in Porto. She didn't use to like coffee, but now she drinks it every day.
grammar_concept.example_translation: Eu costumava viver em Lisboa, mas agora vivo no Porto. Ela não costumava gostar de café, mas agora bebe-o todos os dias.
grammar_concept.common_mistake_pt: Falantes de português tendem a usar o Past Simple sozinho onde o inglês prefere "used to" para deixar claro que já não é verdade ("I lived in Lisbon" só diz que aconteceu, não sublinha o contraste com agora). Também é comum esquecer que a forma negativa/interrogativa usa "did" + "use to" (sem -d): "I didn't used to" está errado, o correto é "I didn't use to".
grammar_concept.correction: "Used to" + verbo base para um hábito/estado do passado que já não é verdade — sublinha o contraste com o presente. Negativa e interrogativa: "did" + "use to" (sem -d no "use"): "Did you use to...?", "I didn't use to...".
grammar_concept.real_world_example: A comparar como a tua vida mudou: "I used to work in an office every day, but now I work from home."

vocabulary.definition_en: something you do often and regularly, sometimes without thinking about it
example_sentences: I used to have the habit of checking my phone first thing every morning.

vocabulary.definition_en: at the present time, in contrast with the past
example_sentences: I used to write letters, but nowadays I only send emails.

vocabulary.definition_en: not anymore; used to be true but not now
example_sentences: He used to smoke, but he no longer does.

exercises.prompt: Complete: I ___ (live) in Lisbon, but now I live in Porto.
exercises.explanation: Hábito/estado do passado que já não é verdade → "used to" + verbo base.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Escrever "use to live" (sem -d) na afirmativa é um erro comum — o -d só desaparece na negativa/interrogativa.

correct_answer: She didn't use to like coffee.
distractors: She didn't used to like coffee.
She not used to like coffee.
exercises.explanation: Na negativa, "did" já carrega o passado, por isso "use to" fica sem -d.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: "Didn't used to" (com -d) é o erro mais comum nesta estrutura.

correct_answer: not anymore; used to be true but not now
exercises.explanation: "No longer" marca que algo era verdade antes, mas já não é.

exercises.prompt: Listen to the audio. What did the speaker use to do every morning?
exercises.explanation: No áudio, ouve-se: "I used to have the habit of checking my phone first thing every morning, but nowadays I no longer do that."
exercises.transcript: I used to have the habit of checking my phone first thing every morning, but nowadays I no longer do that. I leave it in the kitchen instead.

exercises.prompt: Read the text: "My grandfather used to walk five kilometres to school every day. Nowadays, most children no longer walk to school at all." What did the grandfather use to do?
exercises.explanation: O texto indica diretamente: "My grandfather used to walk five kilometres to school every day."

exercises.prompt: Translate to English: "Eu costumava jogar futebol todos os fins de semana."
correct_answer: I used to play football every weekend.
exercises.explanation: "Costumava" corresponde a "used to" + verbo base, para um hábito do passado.
exercises.common_mistake_pt: Traduzir "costumava" só pelo Past Simple ("I played football every weekend") perde a ênfase no contraste com o presente.

steps.content: "Used to" is pronounced as one linked chunk in fast speech: /ˈjuːstə/ — the D of "used" and the initial sound of "to" blend together, so it sounds almost like "yoosta", not "yoozd too".

steps.prompt: Talk about 3 things you used to do as a child that you no longer do now.
Write 5 sentences comparing your life now with how it used to be 10 years ago.
